result.topic_en: Numerical examples showing the rapid convergence of the series connected with the arithmetic-geometric mean M(x,y) and its differential, first for x=√2, y=1, then for the maximal and minimal distances of Jupiter and Ceres.

I. Sit $x=\sqrt{2}$, $y=1$ (Conf. art. 3). Hic habetur $xx-yy=1$
$2(x'x'-y'y')=\frac{1}{2}(x-y)^2=$ 0,0857864376 2690
$4(x''x''-y''y'')=(x'-y')^2=$ 0, ... 3203980 4927
$8(x'''x'''-y'''y''')=2(x''-y'')^2=$ 0, ........ 22 3462
$16(x''''x''''-y''''y'''')=4(x'''-y''')^2=$ 0,
Summa = 0,0861068379 10
Hinc fit $\partial M(x,y)=M(x,y)\times\left\{\frac{\partial x}{2\sqrt{2}}\times 1{,}0861068379\ldots+\frac{\partial y}{2}\times 0{,}9138931621\ldots\right\}$
sive in numeris $=\partial x\times 0{,}460082$[?] .... $+\partial y\times 0{,}5474860839$[?]

Differential of the arithmetic-geometric mean M(x,y) expressed with coefficients obtained from the summed series, numerical example x=√2, y=1
